taxonomy_note: Not every rule BioNexus encodes is an invariant. Each rule declares exactly one epistemic_kind: EXECUTION_INVARIANT, DATA_INTEGRITY_INVARIANT, WARRANT_CONSTRAINT, CALIBRATED_THRESHOLD, HEURISTIC_DETECTOR, or POLICY_DEFAULT. Calibrated thresholds and heuristic detectors must never be presented as universal scientific laws. Legacy INV-xxx identifiers are preserved for certification traceability.

rules.name: pseudoreplication_threshold
rules.description: Minimum number of biological replicates required per experimental condition for pseudobulk differential expression
rules.rationale: With fewer than 2 biological replicates per condition, reliable between-replicate variance estimation is not supported by the intended inferential design. Note the three distinct questions: the software can still compute, the negative binomial model is mathematically defined, but population-level statistical inference lacks a reliable design basis. The value 2 is the minimum at which within-group dispersion becomes estimable, not a universal law of biology.

rules.name: spatial_spots_minimum
rules.description: Minimum number of spatial spots required for neighborhood graph construction and spatial inference
rules.rationale: An engineering minimum for neighborhood graph connectivity: below 5 spots the graph is degenerate and spatial statistics are numerically unstable. This is a calibrated implementation floor, platform- and protocol-dependent, not a cross-platform scientific law.

rules.name: fdr_alpha_threshold
rules.description: Default FDR (False Discovery Rate) alpha threshold for multiple testing correction
rules.rationale: Benjamini-Hochberg FDR control at 5% is adopted as the community-convention default for high-throughput genomics. It is a statistical policy default, legitimately replaceable per study design (e.g. stricter for confirmatory work); BioNexus flags its absence, not a specific alternative value.

rules.name: annotation_marker_consistency_threshold
rules.description: Minimum positive-marker consistency score required for SUPPORTED annotation verdict
rules.rationale: Calibrated balance between sensitivity to true markers and noise tolerance: 0.60 is an engineering choice, not a biological constant. Marker coherence requirements vary with platform, tissue dissociation, and cell-type biology; this threshold must be recalibrated, not universalized.

rules.name: annotation_negative_marker_violation_max
rules.description: Maximum allowed negative-marker violation rate for annotation evidence
rules.rationale: Calibrated tolerance for lineage-exclusive negative marker expression (ambient RNA, doublets, genuine plasticity). 0.20 is a heuristic allowance, platform-dependent; exceeding it suggests but does not prove lineage confusion.

rules.name: annotation_reference_mapping_min
rules.description: Minimum reference mapping score required for independent identity evidence
rules.rationale: Calibrated confidence floor below which reference-atlas mapping is too uncertain to anchor an identity claim. Method- and atlas-dependent; different mapping tools produce non-comparable scores, so this threshold is only meaningful with the documented scorer.

rules.name: annotation_cross_method_agreement_min
rules.description: Minimum cross-method agreement score for independent identity evidence
rules.rationale: Calibrated alternative to reference mapping: independent methods agreeing at >= 0.80 compensate for method-specific biases. The 0.80 value is an engineering judgement about how much agreement substitutes for an atlas, not a statistical theorem.

rules.name: annotation_doublet_rate_max
rules.description: Maximum allowed doublet rate within a labeled population
rules.rationale: Calibrated ceiling reflecting typical doublet rates of droplet platforms (~5-10% at standard loading). 0.15 is platform- and loading-dependent; populations above it MAY be doublet artifacts — the flag is a warning requiring investigation, not a verdict.

rules.name: causal_language_pattern
rules.description: Regex pattern detecting prohibited causal/mechanistic language in scientific claims
rules.rationale: Pattern-based detector with known precision/recall limits: it implements the warrant constraint that causal language exceeds observational evidence classes, but lexical detection can both over-fire (quoted text, negation) and miss paraphrases. The detector is heuristic; the underlying warrant constraint is what carries the science.

rules.name: causal_de_overclaim_patterns
rules.description: Detection patterns for false causal treatment DE claims from marker gene analysis
current_value: caused/induced + N DEGs + without replicates/at single-cell level
rules.rationale: Heuristic detectors for a specific, well-documented overclaim form: marker p-values from single-cell rank_genes_groups cited as causal treatment-condition DE evidence. Detection is pattern-based and falsifiable; review should measure precision/recall on real notebooks.

rules.name: spatial_robustness_ladder
rules.description: Canonical validity ladder for spatial inference verdicts with degradation semantics
rules.rationale: Epistemic grading semantics: ROBUST requires all canonical controls tested+passing AND a permutation null; SUPPORTED requires all provided controls pass without a permutation null; FRAGILE is the honest default when any alternative is UNTESTED; ABSTAIN when a control FAILED or no controls were provided. The ladder structure is a warrant constraint on claim strength.

rules.name: spatial_core_controls
rules.description: Canonical alternative-explanation controls that MUST be addressed before a spatial conclusion can exceed FRAGILE
rules.rationale: The three most common non-biological explanations for spatial enrichment patterns. The requirement to address them before claiming biology is a warrant constraint grounded in spatial-confounding literature; the specific control set is revisable as the field identifies new dominant confounds.

rules.name: spatial_canonical_alternatives
rules.description: Complete registry of canonical alternative explanations for spatial observations
rules.rationale: Registry of known non-biological confounds in spatial transcriptomics. The registry is part of the capability contract and changes only with a contract version bump; individual entries remain open to external review as the field matures.

rules.name: pseudoreplication_detection_pattern
rules.description: Detection logic for cell-level pseudoreplication in differential expression analysis
rules.current_value: BFA-001: DE call at cell level with condition groupby but no pseudobulk aggregation marker
rules.rationale: The underlying science is a warrant constraint: treating thousands of cells from one sample as independent observations inflates false discovery rates. BFA-001 itself is a heuristic detector for that violation (audit-trail pattern matching) with its own false-positive/false-negative profile.

rules.name: cell_type_hallucination_patterns
rules.description: Detection patterns for unverified cell-type assertions from numeric cluster IDs
current_value: concluded that cluster N is/are [cell type]
rules.rationale: Heuristic lexical detectors for asserting cell-type identity directly from unsupervised cluster IDs without marker/reference evidence. The warrant constraint (identity claims need evidence) is sound; the patterns themselves have precision/recall limits subject to review.

rules.name: annotation_verdict_ladder
rules.description: Deterministic verdict ladder for cell annotation evidence assessment
rules.rationale: Epistemic grading semantics for annotation evidence: SUPPORTED requires multiple independent evidence classes to cohere; TENTATIVE indicates partial evidence; ABSTAIN means no evidence, contradictory evidence, or an open-set population. A warrant constraint on identity claims, not a threshold.

rules.name: spatial_coordinate_audit_min_spots
rules.description: Minimum spots threshold for spatial coordinate audit grading
rules.rationale: Calibrated audit floor aligned with the capability precondition for spatial graph construction (INV-002). Same engineering-minimum status: below it the audit grades the input C (fail) because spatial statistics are not supportable, not because the data is corrupt.

rules.name: identifier_namespace_integrity
rules.description: Identifier namespace consistency: joins across feature ID spaces must not silently mix HGNC symbols with Ensembl IDs
rules.rationale: True integrity invariant: cross-namespace joins produce silent one-to-many mappings indistinguishable from correct joins, corrupting every downstream number. Violation must stop execution; no lab policy can relax this.

rules.name: model_substitution_detection
rules.description: Substituting the declared model/backend with another without detection breaks the audit trail (BN-F010)
rules.rationale: Integrity invariant: reproducibility requires that the executed model is the declared model. Silent substitution means the result is not what was advertised; zero silent substitution policy.

rules.name: clinical_diagnosis_without_certification
rules.description: Clinical diagnosis or treatment recommendation without CLIA/CAP-certified validation must be refused
rules.rationale: Execution (safety) invariant grounded in regulation (CLIA 42 CFR Part 493; CAP checklists; EU IVDR 2017/746): uncertified clinical claims directly affect patient decisions. BioNexus escalates this to human/regulatory review under every lab policy.

rules.name: canonical_backend_identity
rules.description: Canonical capability execution requires the declared canonical backend; silent substitution is refused (BN-F010)
rules.rationale: The canonical backend defines the algorithm of a certified capability; executing a substitute without explicit frontier-fallback consent advertises a result the run did not produce. Frontier capabilities retain a documented consent path; canonical ones do not.
